title: From a cube to an octahedron by cutting corners
lede: Slide to cut the corners of a cube deeper and deeper. Halfway you get a cuboctahedron, and at the end an octahedron, the dual of the cube. The counts are recomputed at every position.
notice: Teal faces come from the cube's faces and red faces from the cut corners. The cube's faces shrink to points as the red ones grow to fill the surface.
Vertices, edges and faces change, but V − E + F is always 2, as for every convex polyhedron.
The octahedron has a vertex at the center of each face of the cube, and a face for each corner. Cube and octahedron swap their numbers of vertices and faces.
hint: Drag to rotate. Slide the cut, or use the three shape buttons.
